rationale: The control is styled to look disabled but has no disabled state: it is keyboard-focusable, in the tab order, and has a click handler. As an active component its boundary (2.88:1) must meet 3:1, and it does not.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: the inactive exception applies only to components that are genuinely 'inactive'; an operable control is in scope. (Understanding 1.4.11: 'inactive user interface components')

rationale: aria-disabled='true' alone does not make a component inactive if it remains focusable and operable. The exemption requires genuine inactivity; a component that still works is in scope, and at 2.88:1 the boundary fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: only inactive components are exempt; aria-disabled that does not remove operability does not confer the exemption.

rationale: The glyph is the only thing communicating what the icon-only button does; it is meaning-bearing (required to identify the control), not decorative, so it must meet 3:1. At ~2.5:1 it fails.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: graphical objects 'required to ... identify ... user interface components' are in scope; only truly decorative graphics are exempt.

rationale: The selected-tab underline is a state indicator required to identify the active tab. It is not inactive/decorative, so it must meet 3:1; at ~2.5:1 it fails.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: indicators required to identify component state are in scope.

rationale: This is a custom (role=checkbox) control, not a native default user-agent checkbox, so the default-components exemption does not apply. Its boundary/check at 2.88:1 fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: the exception is for components whose appearance is determined by the user agent; an author-styled custom control is in scope.

rationale: The control is an ordinary active link in its resting state. There is no hover/inactive condition to invoke an exemption; its 2.88:1 boundary fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; G174: active component boundaries need 3:1 in the resting state.

rationale: The field looks muted/read-only but has neither readonly nor disabled set; it is an active input. Its boundary at 2.88:1 fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: only inactive components are exempt; an editable input is active and in scope; G174.

rationale: The hollow ring marks the current step; it is a required wayfinding indicator, not decoration. At ~2.5:1 it fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: graphics required to understand state/progress are in scope.

rationale: The menu item is styled dim but is a real, operable menuitem (focusable, click handler, no disabled/aria-disabled). Its boundary fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: the inactive exemption requires actual inactivity; G174.

rationale: The author may claim the faint look is 'brand-essential', but the divider conveys grouping that could be presented with sufficient contrast; the essential exception does not apply to a mere stylistic preference. If the divider is meant to convey grouping, it is in scope and fails.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: 'Essential' means a particular presentation is essential to the information; a stylistic choice is not essential.

rationale: The focus indicator is a graphical object required to operate the control; it is not inactive/decorative. At 2.88:1 against the page it fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: focus indicators are required to operate components and must meet 3:1; G195.

rationale: The badge's outline is the graphical boundary that identifies it as a distinct status component; required to perceive the badge, it must meet 3:1 and fails at 2.88:1.
The button is genuinely inactive (native disabled attribute: not focusable, not operable). Inactive user interface components are explicitly exempt from 1.4.11.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: 'inactive user interface components ... are not required to meet this contrast requirement.'

rationale: The input is natively disabled (not editable, not focusable); inactive components are exempt.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: inactive components exempt.

rationale: These are default user-agent form controls with no author-supplied visual styling; the default appearance of components is exempt from 1.4.11.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: components whose appearance is determined by the user agent and not modified by the author are not required to meet 1.4.11.

rationale: Natively disabled select; inactive components are exempt.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: inactive components exempt.

rationale: The flourish is purely decorative (aria-hidden, no informational role); decorative graphics are exempt.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: only graphics required to understand content are in scope.

measuredRatioApprox: ~1.1:1 (mark vs white) — exempt as essential brand identity
rationale: Logotypes/brand marks are essential: their specific presentation is required, and WCAG exempts text/graphics that are part of a logo or brand name, plus the essential exception for graphics.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding 'Essential' exception; logotype handling mirrors 1.4.3/1.4.11 logo carve-out.

measuredRatioApprox: selected underline #1a4971 vs white >=6:1; unselected faint underline carries no required info
rationale: The state that must be perceivable (which tab is selected) is shown by the high-contrast underline on the active tab; the unselected tab's faint line conveys nothing required.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: only graphics required to understand state are in scope.

measuredRatioApprox: resting border #1a4971 vs white >=6:1; hover glow not required
rationale: In the resting state the control meets 3:1. The low-contrast effect appears only on hover and is a non-essential enhancement, not a required indicator.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: the required boundary (resting active state) passes; non-required hover decoration is not in scope.

rationale: A custom checkbox is in scope, and here its boundary/check exceeds 3:1.
The control is consistently presented as inactive: aria-disabled, removed from the tab order, and non-operable. As a genuinely inactive component it is exempt.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: inactive user interface components are exempt.

measuredRatioApprox: ~1.1:1 between adjacent swatches (but each numerically labeled)
rationale: Adjacent legend swatches are low contrast to each other, but each carries a redundant numeric label, so the color is not required to read the value and is exempt.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: information also available in adjacent text means the graphic is not required to understand it.

rationale: The focus indicator is the default user-agent ring, not author-styled; default-component presentation is exempt from 1.4.11.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: appearance determined by the user agent and not modified by the author is exempt.
